---
title: "Roadmap and Build Notes"
---

## Recommended writing order

1. `01-mathematical-modelling.qmd`
2. `04-linear-algebra-representations.qmd`
3. `02-statistical-learning.qmd`
4. `03-optimisation-for-ml.qmd`
5. `05-probability-bayesian-uncertainty.qmd`
6. `06-signals-sequences-state-estimation.qmd`
7. `07-information-theory-objectives.qmd`
8. `08-neural-networks-deep-learning.qmd`

## Why this order

- modelling first gives the whole book a common grammar
- linear algebra and statistical learning then establish the two main ML
  viewpoints: representation and inference
- optimisation must land before deep learning
- information theory works better once the reader already cares about losses and
  predictive distributions
- neural networks should arrive after the reader has enough mathematics to see
  them as composed functions rather than as a bag of tricks

## Design guidance

This follow-on book should preserve the house style:

- direct prose
- multiple representations
- visible links back into the main series
- at least one interactive per chapter
- optional domain viewpoints that stay mathematically parallel to the main case

## Structural warning

Do not let the book collapse into a survey of algorithms. It should remain a
mathematics book about data science and AI, not a catalogue of model names.
